questions.question: What is the difference between color and background-color inheritance?
questions.answer: color is inherited, so children use the parent's text color unless overridden. background-color is not inherited, so children are transparent and show the parent's background through.

questions.question: How do linear, radial, and conic gradients differ?
questions.answer: linear-gradient follows a straight angle, radial-gradient radiates from a center point, and conic-gradient sweeps around a center angle. All accept color stops, including hard stops for bands.

questions.question: How do multiple background layers stack?
questions.answer: Comma-separated layers are painted with the first layer on top and later layers beneath. This is how a gradient overlay is placed over a photo without an extra element.

questions.question: What does background-size: cover do compared to contain?
questions.answer: cover scales the image to fill the element, cropping overflow. contain scales it to fit entirely inside the element, possibly leaving empty space.

questions.question: Why use an alpha color instead of opacity for a background?
questions.answer: opacity fades the entire element including text and children and creates a stacking context. An alpha color affects only that color, so text stays fully opaque.

questions.question: Create a hero background with a photo and a dark gradient overlay for readable white text.
Why is background-attachment: fixed risky?
questions.answer: It causes repaint/jank on scroll, performs poorly on mobile, and is often disabled by mobile browsers. Prefer normal scrolling or a fixed-position decorative layer.

questions.question: Why can white text over a photo fail accessibility even when it looks fine?
questions.answer: Contrast varies across the image, so parts of the text may fall below 4.5:1. Add a consistent overlay or panel and verify contrast at the worst spot, not just the average.
